title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck builds the divided-power (PD) envelope of a pair (A, I). This is the universal A-algebra B with a PD-ideal J such that u(I) ⊂ J. He presents it as a polynomial algebra on symbols Γ^n(x) (x ∈ I, n ≥ 2) modulo the standard PD axioms: Γ^n(x+y), Γ^n(xy) and Γ^mΓ^n. He then specialises to A a Z_(p)-algebra, i.e. every prime ℓ ≠ p is invertible in A.

On this page he completes the formula from the previous page. Write n = Σ a_i p^i (0 ≤ a_i ≤ p−1). Then in any PD-algebra
  γ_n(x) = c_n ∏_i γ_{p^i}(x)^{a_i},
where c_n = ∏(p^i!)^{a_i}/n!. This number equals its own prime-to-p part, and so is a unit of Z_(p), because v_p(n!) = Σ a_i v_p(p^i!) (Legendre's formula, with v_p(p^i!) = (p^i−1)/(p−1)).

Consequence: B is generated over A by the elements [x,ν] := Γ^{p^ν}(x), for x ∈ I and ν ≥ 1. He then asks what the relations are, working in A[[x,ν]] with Γ^n defined by the formula above. The relations he lists are:
- Γ^{p^ν}(x+y) is the sum of Γ^{p^ν}x, Γ^{p^ν}y and Σ_{α+β=p^ν} Γ^α(x)Γ^β(y), the last being a polynomial in the generators with i, j < ν.
- Γ^{p^ν}(xy) = x^{p^ν} Γ^{p^ν}(y).
- Γ^mΓ^n = binom(m+n, m) Γ^{m+n}.

The margin asks whether all instances are needed apart from the additivity ones, or whether certain values suffice. The key candidate is
  (Γ^{p^ν}x)^p = ((p^{ν+1})!/((p^ν)!)^p) Γ^{p^{ν+1}}(x),
whose coefficient is p times a p-adic unit.

Finally he starts the monogenic case I = (λ): B is the quotient of A[Γ^n(λ)]_{n≥1} by relations. The page breaks off there; the next page in the archive is unrelated (Néron–Tate style quasi-functions).

The purpose is a concrete presentation of PD-envelopes over Z_(p), as a foundation for crystalline cohomology.
errors: On the previous page the identity is written v_p(n) = Σ a_i v_p(p^ν); it should read v_p(n!) = Σ a_i v_p(p^i!). This is a slip; the formula for c_n on this page is correct.

The question of which relations suffice is left open on the page. In general one cannot drop the multiplicativity relations Γ^mΓ^n for all m, n. Reducing to the p-th power relation (Γ^{p^ν})^p = p·unit·Γ^{p^{ν+1}} also requires the compatibility with x^{p}=p!Γ^p(x) and the additivity relations. No error, but the statement is incomplete.

ideas.what: Construction of the universal PD-algebra (PD-envelope) of (A, I) by generators Γ^n(x) and relations
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), where the PD-envelope is used

ideas.what: Over Z_(p): γ_n = unit · ∏ γ_{p^i}^{a_i} via p-adic digits, using Legendre's formula; the envelope is generated by the γ_{p^ν}(x)
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of divided powers to γ_{p^ν}; Legendre's formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Berthelot; Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology)

ideas.modern_name: Iterated γ_p structure: γ_{p^{ν+1}} = unit·γ_p∘γ_{p^ν}; δ/γ_p-ring viewpoint on PD-envelopes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore (Berthelot; later prismatic and δ-ring literature, Bhatt–Scholze)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine foundational computations for PD-envelopes over Z_(p), all standard in Berthelot's work. The open question about a minimal set of relations is natural but well understood today.
transcription_corrections: The header formula should read c_n = ∏_i[(p^i!)/p^{v_p(p^i!)}]^{a_i} / [n!/p^{v_p(n!)}] = 'partie première à p de' ∏(p^i!)^{a_i}/n!.
The margin reads roughly: 'en faut-il à part pour les Γ^n(x+y), toutes ?' and 'il suffit de ? à part pour certaines valeurs … On a donc … Γ^{p^ν}(x)^p = (p^{ν+1})!/((p^ν)!)^p Γ^{p^{ν+1}}(x)'.
The handwritten page number at the bottom is 32.
